intro: The TFA Matrix exists because of people who share their experiences, expertise, and time. This page acknowledges those contributions. If you've contributed and aren't listed here, please let us know.

groups.name: Framework lead
groups.description: Direction, research, and editorial authority over the framework.

people.name: Em Holyoake
people.role: Founder, Not A Standard — framework author and editorial lead

groups.name: Contributors
groups.description: Research, writing, review, and technical input into specific techniques, tactics, mitigations, or detection indicators.

groups.name: Lived experience
groups.description: People who shared their experiences of technology-facilitated abuse to inform the framework. Contributions are anonymous by default; named acknowledgements only appear here with explicit consent.

groups.name: Practitioner review
groups.description: Specialists in domestic and family violence, digital forensics, law, and mental health who reviewed framework content for accuracy and safety.

upstream.name: MITRE ATT&CK®
upstream.description: The structural model — tactics, techniques, matrices, STIX representation — is adapted from MITRE ATT&CK. The TFA Matrix applies that model to interpersonal harm.

upstream.name: OASIS Open — STIX 2.1
upstream.description: The STIX 2.1 data format that underpins the machine-readable representation of the framework.

upstream.name: Coalition Against Stalkerware
upstream.description: Detection tooling and victim-support guidance referenced in mitigations for monitoring-app techniques.
